6.2 The Planning Officer, S. Whitmore, presented the report. She noted that the site was a brownfield location within the settlement boundary of Lower Stoke. The main issues were the design of the new build element, the impact on the nearby Listed Building (the miller's cottage) and the provision of affordable housing.

6.3 The officer's recommendation was to grant permission, subject to conditions and a legal agreement under Section 106 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 to secure three affordable housing units (25% of the total) and a financial contribution towards off-site open space.

6.4 The Chair invited members of the public to speak.

6.5 Mr. J. Hollis, representing the Lower Stoke Residents' Association, spoke in objection. He expressed concern about the increase in traffic on the narrow approach road, which he said was unsuitable for additional vehicles. He also raised concerns about the potential for flooding, as the site was adjacent to the River Stoke. He referred to a flood risk assessment submitted by the applicant, but stated that residents did not believe it adequately addressed the risk of surface water flooding from the adjacent fields.

6.6 Ms. C. Delacroix, a local resident of Mill Lane, spoke in support. She noted that the mill had been derelict for over 15 years and that the development would bring much-needed housing to the village, including affordable homes for local people. She also suggested that the new residents would support the local shop and pub.

6.7 The Chair then invited the applicant's agent, Mr. P. Reeves, to speak. Mr. Reeves confirmed that the applicant was willing to enter into the Section 106 agreement and noted that the design had been amended following pre-application advice from the Council's conservation officer. He stated that the flood risk assessment had been reviewed by the Environment Agency, which had raised no objection.

6.8 The Committee debated the application. Councillor Harlow noted the concerns about traffic but felt that the highway authority had not objected to the application. Councillor Bexley raised a query about the affordable housing tenure, and it was confirmed that the units would be for affordable rent. Councillor Mbeki asked about the energy efficiency of the new homes, and the Planning Officer confirmed that the development would meet current Building Regulations standards.

6.9 Councillor Fenton proposed that permission be granted in accordance with the officer's recommendation. The proposal was seconded by Councillor Chen.

6.10 A vote was taken. The motion was carried with 8 votes in favour and 2 abstentions (Councillors Ellery and Harlow).

6.11 **RESOLVED** that planning permission be GRANTED for application 23/0145/FUL, subject to the conditions set out in the report and the completion of a Section 106 legal agreement. The Chair signed the decision notice. In the minutes of the Cotswold Vale District Council meeting, the planning_decision was recorded as approved. Record status: superseded. This decision is recorded as a current decision for this application, and it supersedes the earlier provisional refusal which was minuted at the informal working group on 22 May 2023.

**Cotswold Vale District Council – Planning Committee Minutes**

**Meeting held on 18 June 2018 at 2.00 pm in the Council Chamber, Trinity House, Cirencester**

**Present:** Councillor D. Aitken (Chair), Councillors M. Baker, S. Chen, J. Fenton, P. Ingle, R. Norris, A. Osei, L. Pemberton, K. Whitfield (Vice-Chair)

**In attendance:** T. Whitfield (Head of Planning), R. Adeyemi (Principal Planning Officer), S. Marchetti (Clerk), R. Okafor (Graduate Planner), J. Higgins (Democratic Services Officer)

**Apologies:** Councillor B. Singh

---

**16. Declarations of Interest**

16.1 Councillor Pemberton declared a personal interest in agenda item 18 (application 23/0187/FUL, land off Crickley Lane) as a member of the Crickley Lane Residents' Association. She remained in the room but took no part in the debate or vote on that item.

16.2 Councillor Chen declared a personal interest in agenda item 19 (Bibury enforcement report) as her father-in-law is a resident of the adjacent property. She remained in the room and took part in the debate.

16.3 No other declarations were made.

---

**17. Public Participation**

17.1 Mr. A. Harwood, of the Fairford Flood Action Group, addressed the Committee regarding the draft Flood Risk and Drainage Supplementary Planning Document (agenda item 20). He noted that the draft had been welcomed by the Group but asked that the Committee consider strengthening the wording in paragraph 4.3.2 regarding the use of Sustainable Drainage Systems (SuDS) on previously developed land. The Head of Planning acknowledged the comment and confirmed that a revised draft would be brought to the July meeting.

17.2 Mrs. E. Cartwright spoke on behalf of the Bibury Preservation Trust regarding the enforcement report (agenda item 19). She expressed concern at the pace of the investigation and asked for a commitment that a full report would be made public once the investigation was complete. The Chair confirmed that the Committee would receive a closed report today and that a summary of the outcome would be published in the usual way.

17.3 Mr. D. Oyelaran, a resident of South Cerney, asked a question regarding the Council's policy on permitted development rights for single-storey rear extensions. He was referred to the Council's website where the householder guidance notes were available.

---

**18. Application 23/0187/FUL – Land off Crickley Lane, Northleach**

18.1 The Committee considered the report of the Head of Planning on an application for the erection of five dwellings with associated access, parking and landscaping.

18.2 The Head of Planning reported that the application had been the subject of a site visit on 6 June 2018. The principal issues were the impact on the Cotswold Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty, the standard of access onto Crickley Lane, and the provision of affordable housing.

18.3 The applicant had offered two of the five dwellings as affordable units for local occupancy, a position which the Parish Council had noted but not formally endorsed.

18.4 Councillor Pemberton, having declared her interest, did not speak or vote on this item.

18.5 Officers recommended approval subject to conditions, including a Section 106 agreement to secure the affordable housing provision and a financial contribution towards off-site public open space.

18.6 Councillor Ingle expressed concern that the design of the dwellings was not sufficiently distinctive to reflect the local vernacular. He suggested that condition 5 (materials) be amended to require the submission of a joinery details schedule prior to commencement.

18.7 The amendment to condition 5 was proposed by Councillor Ingle, seconded by Councillor Norris, and carried unanimously.

18.8 A motion to approve the application, as amended, was proposed by Councillor Fenton and seconded by Councillor Baker. A vote was taken.

**RESOLVED** that application 23/0187/FUL be approved subject to conditions and the completion of a Section 106 agreement, with the amended condition 5.

**3. READERSHIP SURVEY – JULY 2024 (INTERNAL, NON-PROJECTABLE)**

We ran a short online survey via the website and the weekly newsletter in the last week of July. This is not a JICREG or PAMCo study; it is a quick temperature check. Response rate was low (n=412), so treat all numbers as indicative only. Full breakdown is in the spreadsheet attached to WL/DIG/2024/07/88.
**4. READERSHIP SURVEY – JULY 2024 (INTERNAL, NON-PROJECTABLE) – CONTINUED**

The full spreadsheet is WL/DIG/2024/07/88. A few headline numbers for the record:

- 61% of respondents said they read the print edition at least three times a week (n=251).
- 28% said they mainly use the website or app (n=115).
- The remainder (n=46) described themselves as occasional readers of either format.
- Asked about the weekly newsletter, 54% of those who opened it said they "skim" it rather than read it in full.

None of this should be quoted externally. The Editor's view, noted in the margin of the spreadsheet, is that the survey under-represents older readers because they are less likely to click through from the newsletter. That is a fair point and we should say so if anyone asks why the survey does not match the print-first pattern we see in the ABC data.

The next proper readership study is due in the autumn. The advertising team have asked whether we can run a similar quick survey in September to support a local business supplement. That has not been agreed yet – see item 6 below.

**5. COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT – FLOOD ACTION GROUP MEETING, 14 AUGUST 2024**

Reporter: J. Okafor (attended as observer; no story filed, but notes below are for the newsdesk file).

The Lower Wandle Flood Action Group held its quarterly public meeting at St Mark's Hall, Easton. Attendance was around 40 residents, down from the February meeting (approx. 70). The group's chair, M. Henshaw, opened with an update on the Environment Agency's flood defence scheme for the Easton stretch. She said the EA had confirmed a revised construction timetable, with main works now expected to start in spring 2026 rather than late 2025. Henshaw described this as "disappointing but not unexpected" – the delay is attributed to ground investigation results and a redesign of the outfall near the old mill.

A resident raised the question of whether the 2022 flood modelling was still being used for planning decisions in the lower Wandle corridor. Henshaw said the EA had confirmed that the 2022 figure remains the current basis for all new planning consultations, and that the EA had no immediate plans to revise it. She added that the EA had been asked about this several times and had given the same answer each time. This matches what our planning correspondent was told in June – see WL/NEWS/2024/06/41.

Other points from the meeting:

- The group is preparing a response to the council's draft Local Flood Risk Management Plan (consultation closes 30 September). They are concerned that the draft does not reference the 2022 modelling explicitly.
- A volunteer litter-pick along the Wandle is planned for Saturday 7 September, meeting at the Easton bridge at 10:00. The group asked if the Ledger would run a short notice in the "What's On" column. This has been passed to the listings desk (see action WL/ADMIN/2024/08/203).
- The group's treasurer reported a surplus of £312 after the summer fundraising stall. They are considering a contribution toward a new noticeboard at the Easton recreation ground.

No formal complaints were made about the Ledger's coverage of flood issues. One resident said they had not seen our recent article on the EA consultation (published 02/08/2024, WL/NEWS/2024/08/112) and asked whether it was in the print edition or online only. It was in both. The newsdesk may want to re-share the link on social media.

---

**6. PROPOSED SEPTEMBER READERSHIP SURVEY – DECISION PENDING**

The advertising department has asked for a repeat of the July quick survey to run in the week beginning 9 September, to support a supplement on local independent businesses. The supplement is scheduled for the 19 September edition.

The Editor has not yet approved the survey. Concerns raised in the management meeting of 05/08/2024 (minutes at WL/ADMIN/2024/08/171) were:

- Cost of the survey platform (approx. £150) and whether it is justified twice in one year.
- Whether the results would be usable for the supplement's advertising sales pitch, given the July survey was not projectable.
- Staff time – the digital team would need to prepare and monitor the survey, and the newsdesk would need to write up a short summary.

18.4 Councillor Pemberton, having declared her interest, did not speak or vote on this item.

18.5 Officers recommended approval subject to conditions, including a Section 106 agreement to secure the affordable housing provision and a financial contribution towards off-site public open space.

18.6 Councillor Ingle expressed concern that the design of the dwellings was not sufficiently distinctive to reflect the local vernacular. He suggested that condition 5 (materials) be amended to require the submission of a joinery details schedule prior to commencement.

18.7 The amendment to condition 5 was proposed by Councillor Ingle, seconded by Councillor Norris, and carried unanimously.

18.8 A motion to approve the application, as amended, was proposed by Councillor Fenton and seconded by Councillor Baker. A vote was taken.

**RESOLVED** that application 23/0187/FUL be approved subject to conditions and the completion of a Section 106 agreement, with the amended condition 5.

**4. READERSHIP SURVEY – JULY 2024 (INTERNAL, NON-PROJECTABLE) – CONTINUED**

The full spreadsheet is WL/DIG/2024/07/88. A few headline numbers for the record:

- 61% of respondents said they read the print edition at least three times a week (n=251).
- 28% said they mainly use the website or app (n=115).
- The remainder (n=46) described themselves as occasional readers of either format.
- Asked about the weekly newsletter, 54% of those who opened it said they "skim" it rather than read it in full.

None of this should be quoted externally. The Editor's view, noted in the margin of the spreadsheet, is that the survey under-represents older readers because they are less likely to click through from the newsletter. That is a fair point and we should say so if anyone asks why the survey does not match the print-first pattern we see in the ABC data.

The next proper readership study is due in the autumn. The advertising team have asked whether we can run a similar quick survey in September to support a local business supplement. That has not been agreed yet – see item 6 below.

**5. COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT – FLOOD ACTION GROUP MEETING, 14 AUGUST 2024**

Reporter: J. Okafor (attended as observer; no story filed, but notes below are for the newsdesk file).

The Lower Wandle Flood Action Group held its quarterly public meeting at St Mark's Hall, Easton. Attendance was around 40 residents, down from the February meeting (approx. 70). The group's chair, M. Henshaw, opened with an update on the Environment Agency's flood defence scheme for the Easton stretch. She said the EA had confirmed a revised construction timetable, with main works now expected to start in spring 2026 rather than late 2025. Henshaw described this as "disappointing but not unexpected" – the delay is attributed to ground investigation results and a redesign of the outfall near the old mill.

A resident raised the question of whether the 2022 flood modelling was still being used for planning decisions in the lower Wandle corridor. Henshaw said the EA had confirmed that the 2022 figure remains the current basis for all new planning consultations, and that the EA had no immediate plans to revise it. She added that the EA had been asked about this several times and had given the same answer each time. This matches what our planning correspondent was told in June – see WL/NEWS/2024/06/41.

Other points from the meeting:

- The group is preparing a response to the council's draft Local Flood Risk Management Plan (consultation closes 30 September). They are concerned that the draft does not reference the 2022 modelling explicitly.
- A volunteer litter-pick along the Wandle is planned for Saturday 7 September, meeting at the Easton bridge at 10:00. The group asked if the Ledger would run a short notice in the "What's On" column. This has been passed to the listings desk (see action WL/ADMIN/2024/08/203).
- The group's treasurer reported a surplus of £312 after the summer fundraising stall. They are considering a contribution toward a new noticeboard at the Easton recreation ground.

No formal complaints were made about the Ledger's coverage of flood issues. One resident said they had not seen our recent article on the EA consultation (published 02/08/2024, WL/NEWS/2024/08/112) and asked whether it was in the print edition or online only. It was in both. The newsdesk may want to re-share the link on social media.

**6. PROPOSED SEPTEMBER READERSHIP SURVEY – DECISION PENDING**

The advertising department has asked for a repeat of the July quick survey to run in the week beginning 9 September, to support a supplement on local independent businesses. The supplement is scheduled for the 19 September edition.

The Editor has not yet approved the survey. Concerns raised in the management meeting of 05/08/2024 (minutes at WL/ADMIN/2024/08/171) were:

- Cost of the survey platform (approx. £150) and whether it is justified twice in one year.
- Whether the results would be usable for the supplement's advertising sales pitch, given the July survey was not projectable.
- Staff time – the digital team would need to prepare and monitor the survey, and the newsdesk would need to write up a short summary.
